tagline: Template-based quick editor for social graphics and assets.
verdictSummary: A template-based graphics generator — HTML/CSS templates rendered to PNG, background removal via a local open model, brand colors and fonts applied automatically — is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is Adobe's actual product: licensed stock assets, video and PDF tooling, and deep integration with the rest of Creative Cloud.
coreLoopDIY: A template picker that fills a small set of HTML/CSS layouts with your text, image, and brand colors, rendered to PNG at exact pixel sizes.
whatYouLose: broad licensing coverage for commercial use
whyPeopleStillPay: The content and export ecosystem is already there — templates, stock assets, and format coverage across a dozen use cases — people pay for that breadth, not for the ability to overlay text on an image.
notes: A useful contrast with Canva in this catalogue: a similar template moat, inside a different ecosystem.
prompt:
Build a template-based graphics generator: a small library of HTML/CSS templates for common formats (a square social post, a story size, a header banner, a thumbnail, a quote card), each rendered to a PNG at exact pixel dimensions using a headless browser screenshot. Build a page with a template picker, one input per text field, an image drop zone, and a live preview that renders the same template. Run background removal on uploaded photos with a local open-source model — no paid API needed for this. Load brand settings (two fonts, a handful of colors, a logo) from one config file that every template reads from automatically. Save each export alongside a small sidecar file recording the field values used, so any graphic can be reopened and re-rendered later.

Do not build video or PDF tooling, or a stock-asset library — Adobe's licensed content library is the actual product, and this build assumes you bring your own images.

faq.q: Can I bring in my existing Adobe Express designs?
faq.a: Not directly — Adobe Express doesn't export to an editable format this build can read, only flattened images. A flattened export works as a reference to rebuild from, not an import.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: Not well — filling in a template works in a phone browser, but precise text and image placement is a desktop task, and there's no dedicated mobile app here.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Just hosting for the small web app, typically a few dollars a month or free on a static-friendly host — background removal runs locally with no API cost.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The licensed asset library. Adobe Express bundles stock photos, icons, and fonts already cleared for commercial use; this build hands you empty templates and your own images, with none of that licensing coverage.
